messages.why: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12)
messages.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Mauritania changed by +11.6% per year (95% CI: +9.9% to +12.5%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +6.8% relative to the previous 12 months.

messages.why: classification of 57 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10
messages.text: Of 57 ADM2 units, 41 show significant growth, 16 are stagnating and 0 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Nouakchott accounts for 67% of national light.
Across ADM2 units, light per capita shows neither statistically established convergence nor divergence.

messages.why: clear relationship but only 12 years
messages.text: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 3.30 in levels (95% CI: 2.80 to 3.79, R² = 0.97, 12 years) and 1.68 in growth rates (CI: −0.03 to 3.39). In pseudo-real time (each year predicted from earlier years only), light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of 0.33 (mean absolute error: 2.5 percentage points of growth, no better than the best naive forecast, error ratio 1.14).

messages.why: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 1.97 to 2.37 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection
messages.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.69 in 2025 (no significant change since 2014). About 2.06 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (41% of the inhabited population).

messages.why: 100% of zones confirmed by OpenStreetMap; candidates to be checked
messages.text: 7 candidate industrial zones are detected (3 major hubs, 0 energy sites), covering 5 km². They emit 1% of national light; the largest is Nouadhibou (Dakhlet Nouadhibou). Their light changes by +6.3% per year.

messages.why: OSM coverage varies, lines are undated
messages.text: The mapped grid (OpenStreetMap) totals 2,813 km of line. Between 2014 and 2025, light in towns within 15 km of a transmission line changed by +204%, against +867% beyond 50 km (descriptive: OSM lines carry no dates).

messages.why: blooming understates this share in large cities
messages.text: In 2020, the share of built-up land (GHSL) with no detectable light is highest in Barkéol 79%, Maghama 72%, Tintane 68%: urban expansion runs ahead of electricity service there.

messages.why: few treated towns; event dates of medium/low confidence
messages.text: Event studies (treated vs never-treated towns) — HV connection (6 towns): +0.26 log points, wild-bootstrap p = 0.34; Generation upgrade (12 towns): +0.21 log points, wild-bootstrap p = 0.50.

messages.why: one satellite pass per night (≈01:30): daytime cuts are invisible; 2/4 observable documented episodes detected
messages.text: In Nouakchott, 1.0% of clear nights in 2026 (to 02 Nov) show a citywide drop in light consistent with a power outage (against 1.0% in 2014). The deepest episode starts on 11 Jun 2021: light at 9% of normal, 96% of pixels dimmed.

messages.why: uneven online coverage over time; tone estimated by a model
messages.text: 246 online news articles (FR, AR, EN) cover power cuts in Nouakchott. Coverage peaks in Aug 2026 (42 articles). Most-cited economic themes: Generation capacity & demand, Investment & finance, Heat & air conditioning, Water supply.
2025: extractive sites emit 8% of the country's light; light +85% y/y at the mines, +14% in the rest of the country.
messages.why: cleaned monthly VIIRS; mine coordinates approximate
Sentinel-5P pixels are about 3.5 × 5.5 km: small sites also read the nearby town
messages.text: 2025: NO₂ excess over a 10–30 km ring (µmol/m²) — industrial zones (excl. extractive) +6.4, port areas +2.4, extractive sites +1.3. A national mean cannot show these sites: they cover under 0.1% of the country.
Seaborne trade 2026Q3 (PortWatch): imports +12%, exports +3% year on year (estimated tonnage).
messages.why: AIS ship positions; estimated tonnage, not customs declarations

messages.text: 2025 growing season (July–October): cropland NDVI +43% vs its long-term average; weakest region: Brakna (+29%).
messages.why: METOP NDVI over cropland; harvests also depend on floods and irrigation

messages.text: Elasticity of agricultural value added to growing-season NDVI: 0.18 (1991–2025, p = 0.01).
messages.why: 35 years, HAC errors
ANSADE quarterly accounts
messages.text: Real GDP 2026Q2: +2.8% q/q (SA), +6.6% y/y; excluding gas +5.9% y/y.

messages.why: 6 quarters
messages.text: Best satellite proxy: Port calls (PortWatch) for “Transport” (rank correlation 0.71, same sign 67% of the time).
2026-Q2: unemployment 13.2% (+1.1 pt over a year); youth 14-35 23.5%, women 21.7%. Broad underutilisation (SU4): 34.2%, 47% for youth and 50% for women.
messages.why: ANSADE quarterly survey, ~2,500 households per quarter

messages.text: Reserve for diversification: about 193 thousand unemployed, 39% of them with secondary education; unemployment of tertiary graduates is 17.4%. Labour is available, but few are trained for technical trades.
messages.why: counts estimated (population × survey shares)

messages.text: Students 2023-2024: 65% in social sciences, law, business, arts and humanities; 2.4% in engineering, manufacturing and construction; 79 in agriculture — while the target sectors (mining, gas, hydrogen, agro-food, livestock) need technicians.
messages.why: ANSADE yearbook 2025 (enrolment, not graduates; vocational training not covered)

messages.text: The secondary sector (mining included) produces 32% of value added with 20% of jobs; the primary sector 22% with 25%. Moving workers to more productive sectors is what structural transformation is about.
messages.why: value added from the World Bank, jobs from the ENTE: different sources and years

messages.text: Secondary-sector jobs: 22.6% in 2026-Q2 (+82 thousand over a year). The jump since Q3-2025 (from 16% to 22–25%) needs confirming: construction (gas, infrastructure), mining, or a change in classification.
messages.why: few quarters; shares read from the reports' charts
observed index (NOAA CPC)
messages.text: JAS 2026 RONI: +1.7 °C, a strong El Niño over the rainy season. AGRHYMET (May 2026) puts the western Sahel, Mauritania included, at the highest risk of deficits and dry spells.

messages.why: public sources consulted on 4 November 2026
messages.text: The response runs through the National Response Plan (DCAN, CSA) built on the Cadre Harmonisé, Taazour's Elmaouna transfers and ARC drought insurance. No El Niño-specific plan and no international anticipatory envelope (the FAO–WFP appeal does not cover Mauritania) were identified.

messages.why: censuses
messages.text: Nouakchott holds 29.4% of Mauritanians in 2023 (21% in 1988) and grows 4.2%/yr (2013–2023), against 3.4% for the country.

messages.why: communes: boundaries change between censuses
messages.text: The nine other secondary towns are speeding up: 4.1%/yr in 2013–2023 against 1.7% in 1988–2000; the rest of the country falls from 67% to 59% of the population. Urbanisation is spreading down the urban hierarchy.

messages.why: ANSADE projections on the 2023 census base
messages.text: Towns gain about 91 thousand people a year (3.4%/yr), rural areas 35 thousand (1.5%/yr): every year, the equivalent of a town the size of Kiffa is added to the urban population.

messages.why: 12 towns; buffer around the town
messages.text: Lights move against town growth: rank correlation of -0.41 between 2013–2023 population growth and the growth of the town's own light (2014–2023). Light grows fastest in Tidjikja, Sélibabi, Aïoun: electrification is moving faster than population, so light measures access to power more than town size.

messages.why: ENTE 2026Q2
messages.text: Working-age people are 63% of the urban population against 50% in rural areas: young adults move to the towns, children and older people stay behind.

messages.why: RGPH-5 2023, EPCV
messages.text: 49% of households have electricity in 2023 (20% in 2004): over 90% in Nouakchott, Nouadhibou and Zouérate, under 25% in the two Hodhs, Assaba, Gorgol and Guidimakha. Every new urban resident is a connection to finance.

messages.why: ITU / World Bank
messages.text: 46% of Mauritanians use the internet in 2024 (Senegal 60%, Morocco 91%).

messages.why: voluntary tests: more where there are more users
messages.text: Mobile internet in 2026Q3: 124 Mbps in Nouakchott against 47 Mbps outside the towns.

messages.why: Portulans Institute
messages.text: Network Readiness Index 2025: rank 126 of 127. The 'people' pillar (skills, use) is the weakest (14.5/100).

messages.why: CIVICUS, Internet Society
messages.text: 3 internet shutdowns since 2019, including 22 days without mobile internet in July 2024 after the presidential election, and cuts during the baccalauréat exams.

messages.why: OpenStreetMap: near complete for main roads, incomplete for tracks
messages.text: 44,676 km of mapped roads, 13% in paved classes; 8.8 km per 1,000 people.

messages.why: composite index: ranks tested against other weights, levels are not absolute
messages.text: 35 of 57 ADM2 units are 'critical' (inclusion index below 20), home to 59% of the population.

messages.why: rank correlation, n = 57, p = 0.00; not a causal relationship
messages.text: Better-served ADM2 units are also brighter per person (Spearman 0.68; 0.66 at equal population density).

messages.why: rank correlation with the baseline weights
messages.text: The inclusion ranking changes little with the weights: rank correlation 0.66–0.97 across schemes.

recommendations: Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts.

Share the night-time outage index for Nouakchott with the utility and compare it with its own outage logs (SAIDI/SAIFI): the satellite sees night-time interruptions only, and confirms the large episodes.
Publish regional GDP estimates as experimental statistics, with intervals and a methodological note, after comparison with available regional accounts.
Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is +6 percentage points.
Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

Pair each diversification project (gas, hydrogen, mining, agro-food) with a skills plan: the labour reserve is young, female and has secondary education, while only about 2% of students are in engineering and almost none in agriculture; vocational training (welding, electricity, maintenance, cold chain) is the shortest route.

Prepare the 2027 lean-season response now: use the November 2026 Cadre Harmonisé, pre-position Elmaouna transfers and fodder in the wilayas with the largest rainfall and pasture deficits, and confirm drought-insurance (ARC) coverage.

Plan grid extensions on the census growth of the secondary towns, not only on Nouakchott: Rosso, Aleg and Kiffa grow 5–6% a year, faster than the capital, and every new urban household is a connection and a share of peak demand.

Treat connectivity as infrastructure for diversification: publish the regulator's coverage and quality data next to Ookla's, and avoid national internet shutdowns, which stop mobile money and online services at once.

Target road and service investment with the inclusion index per person, not road density per km²: start with the moughataas that are 'critical' under every weighting tested (section 19b), and map their tracks, clinics and water points in OpenStreetMap first — part of their gap is a mapping gap.

limits.title: What lights measure
limits.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

limits.title: Saturation and blooming
limits.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

limits.title: Gas flares and isolated sites
limits.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

limits.title: Clouds, seasons, moon
limits.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

limits.title: Product breaks
limits.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

limits.title: NTL–GDP elasticity
limits.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

limits.title: Access to electricity
limits.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

limits.title: Administrative boundaries
limits.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.
